identity.title: The Sun at millimeter wavelengths. II. Small-scale dynamic events in ALMA Band 3

paper_type_evidence.quote: ALMA Band 3 data ($\sim 3$ mm / $100$ GHz) with spatial resolution $\sim 1.4$ – $2.1$ arcsec and a duration of $\sim 40$ min are analysed together with SDO/HMI magnetograms.

targets.name: Quiet Sun region near disc centre

question.value: How often do small-scale dynamic brightness-temperature events occur in the quiet Sun in ALMA Band 3, what are their properties, and are they consistent with propagating shock waves?

evidence.quote: An important question in this regard is if the detected signatures are caused by propagating shock waves in the solar chromosphere.
on December 22nd, 2016 (project ID: 2016.1.00423.S)
ALMA Band 3 data ($\sim 3$ mm / $100$ GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four sub-bands: SB1 92-94, SB2 94-96, SB3 104-106, SB4 106-108 GHz

evidence.quote: ALMA receiver band 3 is currently set up with four spectral sub-bands as indicated in Table

angular_resolution.value: clean beam mean ~1.4'' x 2.1'', PA 68 deg

evidence.quote: has a mean value of about $1.4\ensuremath{''}$ and $2.1\ensuremath{''}$ along the minor and major axis respectively, with a beam position angle of $68^\circ$.

observing_dates.value: 22 Dec 2016, 14:19-15:07 UT, four 10-min scans with ~2.5 min gaps

evidence.quote: The observations took place between $14$:$19 \text{UT} - 15$:$07 \text{UT}$ parted in four time scans in blocks of $10$ min each, separated by calibration gaps of $\sim2.5$ min.

provided.value: photospheric LOS magnetograms, 36 s cadence, co-aligned to ALMA

evidence.quote: The magnetograms, measuring the Fe I line (6173 Å) at photospheric heights, have a cadence of $36$ seconds and are co-aligned with the ALMA observations.

provided.value: 170 nm and 30.4 nm channels used for spatial co-alignment

evidence.quote: the ALMA images were cross-correlated with a combination of the $170$ nm and $30.4$ nm channels of the SDO’s Atmospheric Imaging Assembly
The network/inter-network mask by (cite: 2020A&A...635A..71W) is overplotted in Fig.

evidence.quote: reduces the brightness temperature standard deviation $T_\text{b}^\mathrm{rms}$ from $1794$ K to $1254$ K for network pixels

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: RADYN 1D piston-driven acoustic wave simulations, RH 1.5D radiative transfer, 1500 s, 1 s cadence

evidence.quote: The duration of the simulations is $1500$ seconds

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Bifrost 3D MHD simulation with ART code brightness temperature maps, degraded with clean beam

evidence.loc: 4.2 Shock wave propagation in a 3D environment
evidence.quote: the maps are degraded to the resolution of the ALMA band 3 observations by convolution with the clean beam

pipeline_or_manual.value: Solar Alma Pipeline (SoAP); calibration with script delivered with the data from the ALMA Science Archive

evidence.quote: The data set is processed using the Solar Alma Pipeline (SoAP).
data set is calibrated (with a script delivered together with the data from the ALMA Science Archive)
followed by deconvolution using the Multiscale CLEAN algorithm
The pixel size of the final images is $0.32\ensuremath{''}$.

primary_beam_correction.value: applied; output cut at radius 32.8'' (0.3 main beam power response)

evidence.quote: The cut-off point corresponds to 0.3 times the main beam power response.

array_combination.value: interferometric maps feathered with single-dish total power

evidence.quote: These are combined (‘feathered’) with single dish total power measurements.
The specifics of SoAP will be explained in detail in a forthcoming paper (cite: 2020A&A...635A..71W).

unstated_but_needed: SoAP software and version (not public per text), CLEAN parameters, scales, thresholds
Number of clusters k chosen and clustering settings

ART code is in prep. and RADYN/RH run details (grids) incomplete

method.value: SoAP imaging of all sub-bands combined, feathering, Rayleigh-Jeans conversion to Tb, 2 s cadence, 1200 steps

evidence.quote: The final dataset has a cadence of 2 s, with a total of 1200 time steps.
under the assumption of the Rayleigh-Jeans law and formation in local thermodynamic equilibrium

method.value: Box-car smoothing over 7 time steps (14 s); find rise-then-fall peaks with amplitude >= 400 K relative to nearest significant local minimum; lifetime = FWHM

evidence.quote: the data is box-car averaged in time with a size of $7$ time steps $(14\,s)$.
with an amplitude of at least $400$ K

validation.value: conservative criteria to minimize false detections

evidence.quote: the criteria are defined more conservatively for this initial study in order to minimize the number of false detection.

method.value: k-means clustering in space and time within 15'' radius; events fully in one time scan; number of clusters via elbow and silhouette methods

evidence.quote: The pixels showing such a temporary rise in brightness temperature are grouped together using the k-means clustering method
the k-means clustering is only applied to the innermost parts within a radius of $15\ensuremath{''}$.
This method is commonly referred to as the "silhouette method".

analysis_steps.goal: Event statistics and magnetic field comparison

method.value: Size, lifetime, amplitude, base Tb, apparent motion, repetitiveness, HMI LOS field at event location; NW/IN mask

evidence.quote: the apparent motion is estimated for each event.

findings_qualitative.value: Few events in areas with strong photospheric magnetic field; none at |B| > ~250 G

evidence.quote: there are no $T_\mathrm{b}$ peaks at locations with absolute LOS magnetic field strength larger than $\sim 250$ G

claims.hypothesis: Small-scale dynamic events in Band 3 are consistent with propagating shock waves
claims.experiment: Detect events, compare amplitude, lifetime, apparent motion and magnetic field to 1D RADYN and 3D Bifrost predictions
claims.result: 552 events, 450-750 K typical, apparent speeds mostly <10 km/s, low B; 1D amplitudes ~3-4x larger but reduced by beam degradation
claims.finding: Many events plausibly originate in shock waves

evidence.quote: it seems plausible that many of the detected events have signatures originating in propagating shock waves.

claims.hypothesis: Limited resolution reduces observed Tb excess
claims.experiment: Degrade Bifrost maps to clean beam

evidence.loc: 4.2 Shock wave propagation in a 3D environment
evidence.quote: the shock wave shows a signature with a substantially reduced magnitude of $\Delta T_\text{b}=640$ K.

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution limits detection; 552 events is a lower limit

evidence.quote: the $552$ detected dynamical events in this dataset (within $15"$ radius) must therefore be considered to be a lower limit only.

referee_caveats_inferred: Shock identification relies on loose criteria and 1D models
